intro: We use superlatives to show that one thing is above all the others in a group: “the biggest”, “the most expensive”, “the least interesting”. They work like comparatives: -est for short words, most for long words.
objectifs: Form superlatives of short adjectives (the -est) and long adjectives (the most).
Know the irregular superlatives: the best, the worst, the furthest.
Use the right preposition after a superlative: in for a place or group, of for a period or a list.
Use “one of the + superlative + plural noun” and “the least”.

texte: For one-syllable adjectives and two-syllable adjectives ending in -y, add -est and put “the” before it. The spelling rules are the same as for comparatives (lesson 46).
We almost always use “the”, because we are talking about one thing only.

lignes: ends in -w or vowel + -y: no doubling

exemples: Mount Cameroon is the highest mountain in Cameroon.
high → the highest.
Sunday is the busiest day at the market.
busy → the busiest.

texte: For two-syllable adjectives that do not end in -y, and for adjectives with three or more syllables, use “the most” + adjective.
For the opposite idea, use “the least” + adjective, with any adjective: the least expensive, the least difficult.
exemples: This is the most beautiful beach in Senegal.
beautiful: long → the most.
Health is the most important thing.
important: long → the most.
It was the least interesting film of the festival.
the least = the opposite of the most.

texte: Adjectives that are irregular in the comparative are also irregular in the superlative. They are some of the most common words in English.

lignes: She's the best student in the class.
That was the worst day of my life.
Which planet is the furthest from the sun?

sections.titre: In or of after a superlative?
texte: Use “in” before a place or a group seen as one unit: in the world, in my family, in the class, in the team. Do not say “the biggest city of the country”.
Use “of” before a period of time or a list of things: of the year, of my life, of all, of the three.
exemples: He's the tallest boy in his class.
in + group.
It's the biggest city in Canada.
in + place.
It was the happiest day of my life.
of + period.
She's the youngest of the three sisters.
of + list.

texte: “One of the + superlative + plural noun”: the noun is always plural, because you choose from many.
With a possessive, there is no “the”: my best friend, our biggest problem.
Superlative + present perfect + ever: “the best film I've ever seen”. You will see this again with ever / never (lesson 52).
exemples: Brussels is one of the most expensive cities in Belgium.
Plural noun: cities.
My best friend lives in Dakar.
No the with my.
It's the best meal I've ever had.
Superlative + I've ever + past participle.

formule: the + short adjective-est · the most / the least + long adjective · (in + place / group; of + period / list)
prononciation: The -est ending is /ɪst/: biggest /ˈbɪɡɪst/, nicest /ˈnaɪsɪst/, happiest /ˈhæpiɪst/.
“the” is /ðə/ before a consonant sound and /ði/ before a vowel sound: the biggest /ðə/, the oldest /ði ˈəʊldɪst/.
In “the best”, the final t is light and often links to the next word: the best actor /ðə ˈbest ˈæktə/.
Stress the adjective: the MOST imPORtant, the BIGgest.
erreurs: She is the most tall in the family.
She is the tallest in the family.
He's the better player of the team.
He's the best player in the team.
good → the best; and in + group.
It's the oldest building of the city.
It's the oldest building in the city.

dialogue.contexte: Two colleagues, Sami and Julie, are planning a weekend in Bruges and reading reviews online.
lignes: The Canal Inn. But it's also the furthest from the centre.
It's the most expensive, but it has the best reviews in town.
the most + long adjective; good → the best.
What's the most famous thing to see in Bruges?
The Belfry, I think — the medieval tower in the main square. It's one of the most popular sights in the city.
one of the + superlative + plural noun.
That's the most difficult question of the day!

mots: famous
It's the most famous square in Brussels.
known by many people
popular
Football is the most popular sport here.
liked by many people
high
It's the highest mountain in the country.
a long way from the ground; tall
long
The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world.
having a big distance from one end to the other
dangerous
It's the most dangerous road in the region.
able to hurt you
review
This hotel has the best reviews.
an opinion about a hotel, film, book, etc.
choice
This is the best choice for you.
the thing you choose; the act of choosing
ever
It's the best film I've ever seen.
at any time
world
It's the biggest desert in the world.
the earth and all the people and places on it

items: It was the best day ___ the holiday.
She's the oldest ___ my four cousins.
He's the fastest runner ___ the team.
It's the coldest month ___ the year.

exercices.consigne: Put the adjective in brackets in the superlative.
items: That was ___ (bad) film of the year.
Lagos is one of ___ (crowded) cities in the world.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: She's the better singer in the group.
She's the best singer in the group.
Paris is one of the most beautiful city.
Paris is one of the most beautiful cities.
He's the richest man of the country.
He's the richest man in the country.

exercices.consigne: Use the words to write a sentence with a superlative.
items: It's the best restaurant in the town.
it / be (past) / bad / day / my life
It was the worst day of my life.
it / one of / hot / countries / the world
It's one of the hottest countries in the world.

exercices.consigne: Present your town or country in five sentences with superlatives (the biggest, the most famous, the best…).
items: I live in Liège. It's one of the biggest cities in Wallonia. The most famous place is the Montagne de Bueren, a staircase with 374 steps. The best time to visit is in summer. The busiest day is Sunday, when there is a huge market by the river.

a_retenir: Short adjective: the + -est (the cheapest); long adjective: the most + adjective.
Irregular: the best, the worst, the furthest; the opposite: the least.
in + place or group (in the world, in my class); of + period or list (of the year, of the three).
One of the + superlative + plural noun.
With a possessive, no the: my best friend.
